news.title: Medical AI Models May Highlight the Wrong Areas in X-rays, IIIT Hyderabad Study Warns
news.description: A study from IIIT Hyderabad examines the reliability of heatmaps generated by medical AI models for chest X-ray analysis. The research highlights the importance of verifying whether AI-generated explanations focus on clinically relevant regions rather than blindly trusting model predictions. The study received coverage across multiple news publications.

news.title: Fun, Future and linguistics
news.description: A recent feature by Indulekha S in The Hindu explores how technology, linguistics and playful learning are coming together to shape new ways of engaging with language. The journalist also taps into Language Technologies Research Centre (LTRC)'s Parameswari Krishnamurthy's expertise who highlights the role of language technologies in making learning more engaging, accessible and future-ready. https://lnkd.in/dcxUbxY2

news.title: IndicWinoBias: Measuring Occupational Gender Bias and Error Asymmetry in Indian Languages
news.description: We introduce a benchmark to measure occupational gender bias in LLMs across eight Indian languages. Our findings reveal systematic gender bias and higher error rates when the correct referent is female, highlighting the need for multilingual fairness evaluation.

news.title: Per-Category LoRA for Paraphrase Robustness in Medical Vision
news.description: We study how medical vision-language models respond to clinically equivalent questions phrased in different ways. We identify category-specific weaknesses and show that targeted LoRA adaptation can substantially improve paraphrase robustness.

news.title: What Tokens are Learned when Tokenization is Optimized Jointly with Language Modeling?
news.description: We investigate how tokenizer-free models learn token structures across 18 diverse languages and compare them with traditional tokenizers. Our results show a trade-off between morphological alignment and computational efficiency, with tokenization strongly influenced by language typology and script.
